story.title: Authenticate an API client
story.goal: Build the auth header an API client sends, with a key it falls back to when none is passed.
story.catch: The obvious first attempt pastes the key straight into the source. It works — every test passes — because tests check whether code runs, not whether it is safe to ship.
story.steering: The governance gate forbids hardcoded secrets. It catches the key in the diff, reverts the change before it can land, and the run has to do it properly: read the key from the environment.
story.why_it_matters: This is the failure a green test suite will never catch. A key committed once is leaked forever — rotating it is the cheap part, finding every place it reached is not. The gate is what makes 'don't commit secrets' enforceable rather than aspirational.
